sampling.description: Assistant-authored development sample: ten sensor/acquisition, controller/interface, display/LED, low-voltage power, analog, and actuator briefs each, interleaved across families. Not independent user traffic and not release evidence.

briefs.brief: Build a 5 V greenhouse sensor hub that accepts four analog probes on screw terminals and passes an I2C expansion bus through two Qwiic receptacles. Include a controller, a power LED, a fault LED, and four mounting holes for a plastic enclosure.

Build a 12 V irrigation controller with four low-voltage valve outputs on screw terminals and four independently controlled output channels. Include a controller, a USB service connector, and one status LED per zone.

Build a 5 V six-lamp annunciator with six independent current-limited LED channels, six associated pushbuttons, and a controller. Include a USB service connector and four mounting holes for a front panel.
Make a 12 V distribution board for a small test bench, accepting up to 3 A through a two-pin input terminal. Provide four individually fused two-pin output terminals and one power indicator LED.

Create a 5 V strain-gauge bridge interface with a four-pin bridge terminal and a three-pin single-ended analog output header referenced to ground. Include an instrumentation amplifier, adjustable zero trim, and scale the output from 0 to 3.3 V.

Create a dual brushed-DC motor controller for a 6 to 12 V supply and 1 A per motor. Use separate two-pin motor terminals, a five-pin logic header with ground and four drive inputs, reverse-input protection, and a power LED.
Create a 5 V pH-electrode conditioner with a BNC input, a buffered BNC output, and an adjustable calibration control. Add a power LED and keep the board free of microcontrollers.
Make a 12 V dual-fan controller with two PWM control outputs, two tachometer inputs, and a Qwiic temperature-sensor port. Provide a controller, two fan-status LEDs, and two mounting holes.
Create a machine-state display with a Qwiic host connector, a small I2C display, and four current-limited alert LEDs. Add a controller, two buttons, and two mounting holes.
Build a USB-C-powered 5 V field supply board with a 2 A maximum input rating. Route the supply to three locking two-pin outputs, each with a resettable fuse, and add a power LED.

Build a 4 to 20 mA receiver for a 24 V field loop, with a two-pin loop terminal and a 0 to 3.3 V analog output header. Include input transient protection, a precision sense resistor, and an output status LED.
Make a 12 V PWM fan controller for two 4-wire fans, rated for 1 A total fan current. Provide two four-pin fan headers, a three-pin control header, tachometer outputs for both fans, and a power LED.
Make a 3.3 V vibration-sensor bridge with one Qwiic sensor port, one Qwiic host port, and a controller that counts motion events. Provide separate activity and fault LEDs plus two mounting holes.

Design a 5 V wall controller with a differential field bus on a three-position screw terminal, a local controller, and two buttons for operation. Include a bus-activity LED, a fault LED, and four mounting holes.
Design a 5 V twelve-pixel indicator grid in a 3 by 4 rectangle, with a controller and a complete serial LED data chain. Include a USB service connector and two status LEDs.
Create a protected 24 V DC input board for laboratory fixtures at up to 2 A. Include reverse-polarity protection, a replaceable input fuse, a power-good LED, and a two-pin output terminal.

Make a two-channel electret microphone preamplifier powered from 5 V. Each channel needs a three-pin microphone header, adjustable gain, AC-coupled line output on a four-pin header, and a shared power LED.

Build a four-channel low-side solenoid driver for 12 V coils drawing up to 500 mA per channel. Use four two-pin coil terminals, a six-pin logic header, flyback protection on every channel, and individual channel LEDs.
Design a 5 V duct-temperature panel with three thermistor inputs on screw terminals and a small I2C display for local readings. Include a controller, two buttons, and one status LED.
Create a 5 V CAN service adapter with a CAN connector, a switchable terminator, and a USB configuration interface. Include a controller plus transmit and receive status LEDs.
Make a 42 mm circular status beacon with four current-limited LED channels, a controller, and two mode buttons. Power it from 5 V through a USB connector and provide two mounting holes.
Design a 12 V to 5 V converter for a sensor enclosure, rated for 1.5 A at the output. Use separate two-pin input and output terminals, include an input fuse, and show output presence with an LED.
Produce a dual-channel unity-gain line receiver for 5 V operation, with stereo 3.5 mm input and output jacks. Add AC coupling, input protection, and a power LED; do not include a microcontroller.

Design a 12 V linear-actuator H-bridge board for a 2 A actuator. Provide a two-pin actuator terminal, a three-pin limit-switch header, a four-pin logic-control header, reverse-polarity protection, and a fault LED.

Build a 12 V isolated pulse reader with two field inputs on screw terminals and two isolated counting channels delivered to a logic controller. Fit one activity LED per channel and two mounting holes.
Build a 12 V two-motor test jig with two independently controlled low-voltage motor outputs and screw terminals for power and motors. Add a controller, two direction buttons, and two activity LEDs.
Build a Qwiic alarm display with two Qwiic connectors, a small I2C display, three buttons, and three current-limited alarm LEDs. Add a controller and four mounting holes for a wall enclosure.
Make an 18 V DC to 3.3 V logic supply board for up to 800 mA output. Provide a keyed two-pin input, a three-pin output header carrying 3.3 V and ground, reverse-input protection, and a status LED.

Design a four-channel 3.3 V thermistor interface with four two-pin sensor terminals and a five-pin analog output header. Each channel must provide a bias resistor and RC filtering, with a separate channel label at each terminal.

Create a 12 V stepper-driver module carrier for a plug-in driver module and one four-wire motor. Include a four-pin motor terminal, a six-pin logic header, three microstep-select jumpers, and a power LED.
Create a solar-irradiance reader for a 0 to 10 V sensor, with the sensor on a BNC connector and a controller reporting the acquisition over a Qwiic port. Run it from 5 V and include a power LED.

Make a 5 V I2C output module with two Qwiic connectors and eight independently controlled low-voltage outputs on screw terminals. Include a controller or GPIO expander, eight output LEDs, and four mounting holes.
Create an eight-cue LED bar with eight current-limited indicator channels, a controller, and four cue-select buttons. Include a USB service connector and two mounting holes.

Produce a 5 V distribution panel for two USB-powered instruments with a 2 A total input limit. Give each instrument its own fused two-pin output and independent output-present LED, using a common two-pin input terminal.

Build a 3.3 V piezo impact-sensor interface with a two-pin piezo terminal and one analog output header. Protect the amplifier input against positive and negative piezo excursions, provide an adjustable gain trimmer, and add a trigger LED.
Make a 6 V servo-power injector for four hobby servos with a 3 A input rating. Provide four three-pin servo headers, a two-pin power terminal, one resettable fuse per servo output, and a power LED.
Make a 5 V hall-effect tachometer board with two screw-terminal sensor inputs and two independent pulse-count channels. Add a controller, two status LEDs, and a USB service connector.

Design a 5 V four-channel pulse generator with four logic outputs on a header and four independently adjustable output channels. Provide a controller, two buttons, a USB service connector, and a power LED.

Design a 5 V serial front-desk display with a differential serial input on a three-position screw terminal, a small local display, and a controller. Include receive and fault LEDs plus two buttons for acknowledgement.

Build a 9 V load-switch board for a 1 A accessory, with a two-pin input and two-pin load output. A three-pin logic header must enable the load, and the board needs reverse-polarity protection plus an enabled indicator LED.

Create a 0 to 10 V process-input conditioner that runs from a 12 V supply and produces a 0 to 3.3 V output. Use a two-pin field terminal, a three-pin power header, input protection, and a filtered analog output header.

Build a two-channel 24 V valve pulse driver for coils drawing up to 750 mA each. Use separate two-pin valve terminals, a four-pin trigger header, flyback protection, and a visible LED for each active valve channel.
Build a rain-gauge logger with a 5 V supply, one screw-terminal tipping-bucket input, and a Qwiic connector for an external display or logger. Include a controller, a pulse LED, and a reset button.
Build a USB macro keypad with twelve buttons, a controller, and twelve independently scanned key channels. Include three status LEDs and four mounting holes for a desktop shell.

Make a four-zone tabletop scoreboard with four independent display zones, four mode buttons, and a controller. Use four current-limited status LEDs for zone markers, add a USB service connector, and provide four mounting holes.

Create a 12 V, 2 A distribution board with two switched two-pin outputs for a camera rig. The second output must be held off until the first is enabled, both outputs need resettable fuses, and each output needs its own LED.

Make a 5 V photodiode transimpedance amplifier board with a two-pin detector connector and a buffered analog output header. Include a switchable feedback-gain jumper, a 10 kHz low-pass filter, and a power LED.

Produce a 12 V DC pump controller for a 2 A pump with a two-pin pump terminal and a three-pin command header. Add a current-sense analog output, reverse-polarity protection, a flyback path, and a running indicator LED.
Design a 5 V load-cell front end with a four-wire screw-terminal bridge input, an analog buffered output, and a Qwiic digital readout port. Fit a calibration button and a power LED.
Create a 12 V timed-valve controller with two screw-terminal outputs, two independently timed control channels, and a Qwiic port for a display. Fit a controller, two buttons, and two zone LEDs.
Build a hexagonal alert tile with six current-limited LED channels, a controller, and one Qwiic connector for upstream commands. Include one button, a power LED, and two mounting holes.

Make a 24 V input to isolated 5 V output interface supply using a DC-DC module, with 500 mA output capacity. Use separate two-pin terminals for input and output, retain isolated returns, and provide an output-present LED.

Build a 9 V high-impedance guitar input buffer with one 6.35 mm input jack and one 6.35 mm output jack. The circuit must be unity gain, AC-coupled at the output, and include reverse-polarity protection with a power LED.

Create a 5 V encoder interface for one quadrature motor encoder, with a six-pin encoder input and a six-pin buffered output header. Include 3.3 V-compatible output levels, RC input filtering, and a power LED.

Create a four-channel 4 to 20 mA loop monitor powered from 12 V, with four screw-terminal sensor inputs and four digitized acquisition channels. Include a controller, two status LEDs, and four mounting holes.

Make a 5 V addressable-sign controller with a Qwiic host port, one digital LED-strip output connector, and a controller driving sixteen LED data positions. Include a USB service connector and two status LEDs.

Create a panel-label reader with a small I2C display, a controller, a rotary encoder, and two navigation buttons. Add a Qwiic host connector, two status LEDs, and four mounting holes on a rounded-rectangle board.

Design a 12 V accessory power board that supplies one regulated 5 V, 1 A output and one protected raw 12 V, 1 A output. Use a common screw-terminal input, separate two-pin output terminals, a master fuse, and LEDs for both rails.

Produce a two-channel analog anti-alias interface for 3.3 V data loggers. Put each input on a two-pin terminal and each filtered output on a shared five-pin header, with a 1 kHz low-pass corner and a power LED.

Build a four-channel 5 V vibration-motor driver for motors drawing up to 150 mA each. Use four two-pin motor headers, a six-pin logic header, flyback protection, and one activity LED per motor channel.
